entries.title: We’re bringing AI Brief to more languages and adding a new AI Max reporting feature.
entries.summary: We’re making it easier to create great AI Max campaigns by adding a new reporting feature and bringing AI Brief to more languages.
entries.content:
We’re rolling out new AI Max features that provide advertisers with greater control and new reporting to understand performance.

First, we’re bringing the closed beta of AI Brief to more languages: Dutch, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, and Spanish. AI Brief lets you guide AI Max in your own words with detailed context on your business, audience, and key messaging.

Second, we’re introducing a new reporting feature in Google Ads to give you a clearer view of AI-driven performance. It will show a single, unified view of the Search ads journey — making it easy to see what search terms triggered your ads, which creative assets the user saw, and exactly where they landed on your website. This precise interface will help you better understand how customers interact with your business and validate the strategic value AI Max brings to your campaigns.

We’ll share additional details and availability later this year.

entries.title: Google and the Gates Foundation to bring AI resources to 200 million farmers across the Global South.
entries.summary: Smallholder farmers produce nearly 35% of the world’s food across more than 500 million farms, yet they often lack access to the satellite data, financial services, and …
entries.content:
Smallholder farmers produce nearly 35% of the world’s food across more than 500 million farms, yet they often lack access to the satellite data, financial services, and public support that can help them prepare and respond to increasingly unpredictable weather.

To help bridge this gap, we've partnered with the Gates Foundation to direct $100 million to organizations that scale AI-powered climate and crop insights to 200 million smallholder farmers across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia — up from 50 million. This combined funding and dedicated technical support from Google researchers will help deploy real-time climate, agricultural, and language AI tools. Learn more.

entries.title: Investing in global talent and AI literacy
entries.summary: A woman typing at a computer in a computer lab
entries.content:
Every day on Google Search, people turn to variations of the same question: “How do I get started with AI?” In our work across both the United Nations and Google, we see that question everywhere.

People around the world are eager to use these tools, but finding a clear starting point can be daunting. Global research from Ipsos and Google shows that hands-on training makes people up to four times more likely to become confident with AI. Practical training is what turns an unfamiliar technology into something genuinely useful every day, whether you’re an educator planning coursework, a municipal worker improving public services, or a job seeker building your resume.

Making those everyday wins possible for everyone was a central focus at this year’s United Nations General Assembly in New York. The International Telecommunication Union (ITU) estimates that 1.2 billion people worldwide still need training to acquire basic digital skills, while another 311 million need training to develop above-basic skills. Connectivity is essential, but connectivity without the capabilities to participate in an AI-powered economy risks creating a new divide.

That is why we need to move with both scale and speed, bringing governments, technology companies, learning providers and international organizations together to make high-quality AI learning accessible to everyone, everywhere.

To turn that shared commitment into tangible action, Google is providing 100,000 scholarships through the AI Skills Coalition, a partner-led initiative under ITU’s AI for Good program that brings together governments, industry, academia, UN organizations and civil society to collectively expand access to AI skills and accelerate inclusive and responsible AI adoption.

The 100,000 scholarships will complement over 200 courses in the Coalition catalogue for participants across more than 80 countries, in support of the ITU-UNICEF Giga initiative, a joint initiative by ITU and UNICEF to help governments connect every school, bringing vital online resources to communities around the world.

Every country and community faces unique opportunities, so local leaders and national ministries will have the flexibility to tailor the training to their workforce priorities. The training provides:

  • Practical, everyday skills: Hands-on practice, requiring zero background in technology.
  • Credentials that open doors: Recognized certificates taught by experts so learners can demonstrate their mastery to employers
  • Locally led programs: Designed to support national workforce priorities, including students, teachers, job seekers, entrepreneurs, small business owners and civil servants.

Bridging the global skills gap isn’t something any single organization can achieve on its own. It takes governments, international institutions, and technology providers working hand-in-hand to ensure opportunity is shared by all.

Through the AI Skills Coalition, we will track scholarship activation and utilization, learner participation and completion, certificates earned, and the reach of priority groups, including youth, educators, public servants and job seekers. We will also work with participating countries to understand how learners apply their new skills in education, employment and public service, generating evidence on what works and helping us continuously improve in providing AI options for learners around the globe.

Our goal is straightforward: to answer that everyday question, “How do I get started with AI” with clear, high-quality pathways for everyone.

Learn more at grow.google/ai.

entries.title: Using AI to help local governments connect with constituents
entries.summary: Illustration of a crowd of people in front of the white house with various text bubbles
entries.content:
A year ago, Jigsaw, a tech incubator within Google, launched Sensemaking AI: a suite of open-source tools designed to help public leaders deliver on policies and programs that reflect the needs of their communities.

Today, as part of Google.org’s commitment to help governments use AI to improve public services, we’re supporting the new Jigsaw Partner Program with a collaborative fund to help more policymakers benefit from AI-powered civic conversations — and calling on local government leaders around the world to join us.

Through the new Jigsaw Partner Program, localities can use AI to run fast, large-scale civic conversations at no operational cost, surfacing insights about community needs that can help shape essential services. Cities are already seeing results: in Bowling Green, Kentucky, input from 8,000 residents informed a 25-year growth plan, with similar initiatives underway in Chattanooga, Tennessee, Riverside, California, Kitchener, Ontario, and more. Civic leaders have shared that Sensemaking AI helps them hear from everyone to make more informed policy decisions.

Google.org is joining forces with leading philanthropic institutions, including Bloomberg Philanthropies and the David & Lucile Packard Foundation, who will support efforts to further expand the potential of these tools in municipal contexts.

Civic leaders can’t govern effectively in the dark, and constituents shouldn't have to shout to have their voices heard. We invite governors, mayors, and local officials globally to express interest in using Sensemaking AI through the Jigsaw Partners Program. Together, we are building a future where hearing from every voice isn't just an aspiration, but the baseline for effective leadership.

entries.title: Expanding free AI training for educators
entries.summary: Badges in blue, red, orange, green with gradients representing Google AI Educator Series
entries.content:
This week, at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City, we’re meeting with leaders to discuss the future of learning and education, including important topics like how AI can enhance classroom teaching while keeping educators at the center of learning. At the Fostering the Future Together Partnership event, hosted by First Lady Melania Trump, we announced that Google.org is supporting Digital Promise, a nonprofit working to expand opportunity for each learner. This funding will help bring practical AI skills to more teachers, schools, and higher education institutions.

Expanding access to practical AI skills for teachers

Earlier this year, we announced our plans to provide free, comprehensive AI training to all 6 million K-12 teachers and higher education faculty in the U.S. Designed and built in partnership with ISTE using a "teachers teaching teachers" approach, the training focuses on foundational, transferable AI skills, instructional judgment, and practical applications that apply across various AI tools for lesson planning and productivity. Through self-paced e-learning modules, educators can earn recognized digital badges that showcase their commitment to continuous learning.

With today’s support, Digital Promise will develop scalable models and frameworks to help more teachers access high-quality, hands-on AI professional development.

  • Helping teachers learn AI skills at scale: Digital Promise will work with state education agencies and school districts to offer tailored training and support teacher networks that build long-term AI skills.
  • Supporting community college faculty: Community colleges are vital for job preparation. Digital Promise will partner with community college systems to help instructors learn ways to incorporate AI into their daily work and teaching.
  • Sharing open research and practical guides: Over the next two years, Digital Promise will study what helps college faculty use AI effectively. They will publish a free, public guide to help higher education institutions anywhere adopt AI thoughtfully.

Educators, school leaders, and faculty can explore the free Google AI Educator Series and start earning digital badges today on the Google for Education Learning Center.

entries.title: Googlebook’s built-in intelligence reinvents the way you use your laptop
entries.summary: A Googlebook with text reading: "Designed for Gemini Intelligence"
entries.content:
Great hardware needs software that can actually keep up, so we designed Googlebook with an intelligence system that brings Gemini directly on your device. It anticipates what you need, simplifies your daily tasks, and proactively helps you get things done. Here are a few features that make Googlebook uniquely helpful.

Work smarter with Magic Pointer.

Magic Pointer reinvents the decades-old point and click computer experience.

With a quick wiggle of your cursor, Magic Pointer — which understands text, images, and context — brings Gemini exactly where you’re working and makes previously tedious tasks trivial. Here are just a few examples of how you can use Magic Pointer.

  • Instant scheduling: Highlight a complex marathon training plan on a web page, and ask Gemini to automatically map out those runs and schedule them in Google Calendar.
  • Keeping you secure: Hover over a suspicious email and ask Gemini to analyze the text and images to verify if it’s spam or a legitimate message.
  • Combining visuals: Select a set of images with Magic Pointer and ask Gemini to visualize them together. No downloading, uploading, or prompting. Just point, ask, result.

From day one, we built Magic Pointer with privacy at the core. It only springs into action when summoned by a wiggle, and stays off when you’re not using it.

Talk naturally to your Googlebook with Rambler.

Standard voice dictation writes down everything that comes out of your mouth — including the stutters, mistakes, and filler words. And cleaning those up can take longer than typing your thoughts on your keyboard. Rambler actually understands the context and nuance behind your words.

Say you’re drafting team meeting notes when you’d rather be wrapping up your day. Just open Rambler and let your stream of consciousness fly. Rambler will take a disorganized verbal brain dump and clean up the errors, organize action items into structured bullet points, and even add relevant emoji. It’s also natively multilingual, so you can switch languages mid-sentence without losing a beat.

Make Googlebook your own with Create My Widget.

Create My Widget on Googlebook lets you build your own widgets, with no coding experience required. Build bespoke widgets simply by describing what you want. Make one to track your favorite sports team’s scores, or create a visual countdown to your next family trip.

If you want to go further, Google Antigravity comes with every Googlebook. Use it to write your own apps then deploy them directly to your Googlebook. Developers also have access to a full Linux terminal environment to run tools like Claude Code or Antigravity CLI and do serious agentic coding right on your Googlebook.

Get started right away with Gemini and Chrome.

The powerful Gemini features that you know and use on Chrome and Android are available on Googlebook out of the box, including task automations, Gemini Live, and proactive suggestions that show your next move based on what’s on your screen. You can even close your laptop while Gemini Spark works in the background to process complex requests and finish your tasks.

Pricing, availability, and pre-order details

Starting at $899, every Googlebook includes 12 months of Google AI Pro providing 5TB of cloud storage and higher usage limits in Gemini, plus 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. Googlebook OS also comes with regular feature drops and updates for up to 10 years.

Pre-orders are now open on the Google Store, Best Buy, and other select retailers. Devices hit shelves on October 4 in the U.S., and October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.

entries.title: Premium materials and striking design set Googlebook apart
entries.content:
Beautiful on the outside and powerhouses on the inside, Googlebook sets a new standard for hardware. Here’s what to expect from our new category of premium laptops.

Five distinctive models

Premium hardware shouldn’t be one-size-fits-all, so we’re launching five flagship models built with the world's best laptop makers, starting at $899.

Master craftsmanship

Every Googlebook is made from premium materials like aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber, making them exceptionally light, sleek, and durable. They feature touchscreens with up to 2.8K resolution that are bright enough to view outdoors in direct sunlight without a glare.

Our partners spent months fine-tuning the features that you engage with most.

  • Custom keyboards: backlit layouts designed for fast, clean typing
  • Haptic trackpads: large, glass-feel surfaces with precise haptic feedback and native OS gesture support
  • Cinematic audio: up to six speakers with Dolby Atmos surround sound, paired with studio-quality, background noise-canceling microphones

Interactive Glowbar design

We’re bringing back the Glowbar, which dances when you boot up, sweeps to show battery level, and supports other playful patterns. We’re also opening Glowbar access to developers to build custom, interactive animations.

Silent, next-gen power

We teamed up with Intel, Qualcomm, and MediaTek to ensure Googlebook keeps up with developers and creators alike.

At launch, you can choose between Intel Core Ultra Series 3 and Snapdragon X Elite processors, which are paired with advanced NPUs running at over 45 TOPS of on-device AI power. This lets you run complex AI workflows without spinning loud and disruptive fans.

  • Memory: a baseline of 16GB of high-speed RAM across the entire portfolio, and some models go up to 32GB
  • Battery: up to 14 hours of video playback and 16 hours of web browsing

Pricing, availability, and pre-order details

Starting at $899, every Googlebook includes 12 months of Google AI Pro providing 5TB of cloud storage and higher usage limits in Gemini, plus 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. Googlebook OS also comes with regular feature drops and updates for up to 10 years.

Pre-orders are now open on the Google Store, Best Buy, and other select retailers. Devices hit shelves on October 4 in the U.S., and on October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.

entries.title: Googlebook: The laptop your Android phone has been waiting for
entries.content:
Googlebook — a new category of laptops designed for the way we work today — is now available for pre-order. Built on the Android technology stack and paired with desktop foundations from ChromeOS, Googlebook is designed for Gemini Intelligence and engineered to work with your Android phone right out of the box.

Today, we often switch between starting tasks on our phones and finishing them on our laptops. To make that experience better for Android users, we teamed up with the best laptop makers in the industry to deliver top-tier hardware alongside Google software that connects effortlessly with your phone.

Premium hardware from leading partners

Our initial selection of flagship devices are built by Acer, ASUS, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, offering you choices that fit your style.

Starting at $899, every Googlebook features premium materials like aluminum, magnesium alloy, and carbon fiber. You’ll find responsive touchscreens with up to 2.8K OLED displays, haptic glass trackpads, and backlit keyboards. Under the hood, top-of-the-line processors from Intel and Qualcomm — paired with dedicated NPUs capable of over 45 TOPS — deliver snappy on-device performance and up to 14 hours of battery life.

We’re also bringing back a familiar favorite: the Glowbar. Positioned cleanly on the exterior, it lights up at startup, sweeps to show your battery charge level, and reacts with playful animations when you talk to Gemini.

The companion your phone has been waiting for

If you use an Android phone, your laptop shouldn't treat it like a stranger. Googlebook is built on a shared Android foundation, so your phone and laptop work seamlessly together

It starts with setting up your device. When you sign in, your Android phone’s settings, saved passwords, Wi-Fi networks, and messages will move with you, backed by end-to-end encryption. Once you’re set up, Googlebook makes it easy to move between your phone and laptop and back to get things done.

  • Continue On: Pick up exactly where you left off on your phone, right on your laptop. If you start a project in BandLab on your phone while commuting, you can open your Googlebook and continue right from the taskbar.
  • Files: Rather than hunting through downloads or emailing attachments to yourself, use your Googlebook’s Files app to view, search, and open files and photos from your phone.
  • Cast My Apps: Need to order dinner from a delivery app or grab a one-time code from Messages? Cast My Apps lets you stream and interact with your phone’s apps in a desktop window without interrupting your workflow.

Helpful intelligence built into the desktop

Googlebook is designed for Gemini Intelligence to simplify your workflow.

  • Magic Pointer: Wiggle your cursor to bring Gemini directly to whatever’s on your screen. You can ask Gemini to organize a messy calendar or translate text without juggling multiple windows. Gemini only acts when you ask it to, and you can switch it off whenever you want.
  • Rambler: Located right next to the Quick Insert key, Rambler turns spoken thoughts into organized, ready-to-share writing. Talk through your notes, action items, or a stream of consciousness — even in multiple languages — and Rambler structures them with clean headers, checklists, and formatted takeaways.
  • Create My Widget: Customize your desktop by describing what you need in plain language. Create My Widget generates custom widgets that can share relevant updates throughout your day.

The full web, plus your favorite apps and tools

Googlebook brings together the best of the web and the Play Store.

You get the desktop-class Chrome browser with extensions alongside millions of Android apps, many of them optimized for large screens, mouse and keyboard input.

Run native creative tools like Adobe Photoshop, Adobe Lightroom, and CapCut, or watch shows on popular streaming platforms like Netflix and HBO Max with offline viewing supported. When it’s time to unwind, explore thousands of Android games or play AAA PC titles you own with a complimentary year of GeForce NOW included with every purchase.

For builders and makers, Googlebook includes Antigravity, our AI agent development platform, allowing you to build, test, and deploy apps right on your device. Developers also get a full terminal environment to run tools like Claude Code or Antigravity CLI and perform serious agentic coding.

Modern, secure software architecture

Googlebook is built on the same security architecture as ChromeOS, anchored with our Google Titan hardware root of trust, defense in-depth architecture, and on-device malware detection. This means you get the security of industry-leading protection for all your personal data from day one.

It also features a first for the laptop category: a Level 5 security-certified pKVM hypervisor. This hypervisor powers an isolated Linux environment with a full terminal access, so you can safely run any Linux developer tools, pull code repositories, or execute autonomous agents.

Pricing, availability, and pre-order details

Starting at $899, every Googlebook includes 12 months of Google AI Pro providing 5TB of cloud storage and higher usage limits in Gemini, plus 3 months of YouTube Premium, Adobe Photoshop, and more. Googlebook OS also comes with regular feature drops and updates for up to 10 years.

Pre-orders are now open on the Google Store, Best Buy, and other select retailers. Devices arrive on shelves starting October 4 in the U.S., and October 5 in Canada, the U.K., Ireland, France, Germany, and Australia.

entries.title: Earn continuing education and college credits for AI educator training.
entries.summary: Earn college or continuing education credits by taking the Google AI Educator Series courses.
entries.content:
The Google AI Educator Series, our bite-sized, 15-minute training sessions for educators, now has a new way coming to showcase what you’ve learned:

  • Undergraduate credit: Participants will be able to earn fully-accredited, undergraduate college credits at no cost through our partnership with College Unbound, which can be counted towards BA completion or converted to CEUs.
  • Graduate credit: And thanks to our partnership with ISTE and Dominican University, educators will also be able to turn their new AI skills into fully accredited, graduate-level college credits.
  • Continuing education credit: Educators and administrators in Illinois will be able to earn hours toward their license renewal through our partnership with the Illinois Digital Educators Alliance.

To start earning credit today, join the Google AI Educator Series Badge-a-thon, a flexible, drop-in festival on September 19. Join our 12 hour webinar at any time to watch live educator demos, learn time-saving tricks, and earn ISTE-aligned digital badges. Register today at goo.gle/GESBadgeathon.

entries.title: New experts join Google’s AI & Economy team
entries.summary: Text "AI & Economy Research Program" all over a green grid background, with the Google G logo in the bottom right corner
entries.content:
We recently launched the AI & Economy ATLAS v1.0 and its interactive open-access site to understand how people are using Google’s AI tools at work and in their daily lives. But tracking adoption patterns is only the beginning. As artificial intelligence reshapes jobs, businesses, and everyday lives, navigating this shift requires a multidisciplinary approach that unites fine-grained data with rigorous economic inquiry.

To further help organizations, workers, researchers, and policymakers make sense of this complex transition, we are expanding our AI & Economy Research Program, and welcoming world-class economists to help build and lead this work.

Technological shifts are rarely instantaneous. Our program measures and analyzes this evolution in real time, focusing on core areas including the future of work, productivity and growth, global technology diffusion, and AI’s impact on scientific discovery.

Expanding our scientific expertise and engagement

Executing a research agenda of this scope requires deep collaboration among academia, industry leaders, and policymakers. To expand our scientific capacity and engage more deeply with these diverse stakeholders, we are bringing together leading external advisors, visiting scholars, and dedicated research program leadership. Joining us as Academic Advisors and Visiting Fellows:

  • Philippe Aghion, Academic Advisor: Professor Aghion, 2025 Nobel Laureate in Economics and the Kurt Björklund Chaired Professor at INSEAD and the Collège de France, joins our advisory group alongside Nobel Laureate Michael Spence and Cambridge’s Dame Diane Coyle, applying his pioneering work on innovation-led growth and creative destruction to model AI's long-term macroeconomic trajectory.
  • Ajay Agrawal, Visiting Fellow: Professor Agrawal joins our Visiting Fellows program, where he will collaborate closely with David Autor, a current Fellow and head of MIT’s Department of Economics. Professor Agrawal, who holds the Geoffrey Taber Chair in Entrepreneurship and Innovation and is a Professor of Strategic Management at the University of Toronto’s Rotman School of Management, will advance our core research on the economics of AI and scientific discovery, AI and robotics, and how AI can expand the frontier of human welfare.

To steer empirical projects and integrate insights across our agenda, we are also introducing two renowned researchers as Directors of Google’s AI & Economy Research Program:

  • Anu Madgavkar: Formerly a Partner at the McKinsey Global Institute (MGI), Madgavkar joins Google following a two-decade career leading global research on labor markets, technology adoption, and structural economic transitions. She has frequently advised governments, multilateral institutions, and business leaders worldwide, contributing regularly to the World Economic Forum and the United Nations. At Google, she will lead empirical research on global AI diffusion, small business ecosystems, and the workforce impacts of generative AI.
  • Daniel Rock: Joining from the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, Professor Rock is a leading economist on AI and labor, having co-authored foundational papers on technological transitions. An AI2050 Early Career Fellow and MIT Digital Fellow, he will lead Google's empirical research, bridging frontier model telemetry with rigorous econometrics to analyze enterprise productivity, labor restructuring, and scientific discovery.

Anu Madgavkar and Daniel Rock will lead Google's AI & Economy Research Program alongside Alex Imas, Director of AGI Economics at Google DeepMind, and Zanna Iscenko, AI & Economy Lead, in Google's Chief Economist's Office.

Shaping future research and collective impact

Maximizing AI’s economic opportunity while mitigating disruption requires sustained partnership. This expanded team of experts will serve as a scientific bridge, directly informing future ATLAS updates and empirical research.

Together, we will focus on identifying the organizational practices, public policy frameworks, and training programs needed to ensure AI upskills workers, democratizes expertise, and drives broadly shared prosperity.

To learn more, read our latest research publications, and interact with our latest global data, visit ai.google/economy.
